questions.prompt: n = 5, Σx = 26, Σy = 353, Σx² = 158, Σy² = 25565, Σxy = 1956. Compute Pearson r (3 decimals).
questions.explain: Numerator: 1956 − (26)(353)/5 = 120.4. Denominator: √[(158 − 26²/5)(25565 − 353²/5)] = √[(22.8)(643.2)] = 121.099. **r = 0.994** — very strong positive linear relationship between hours studied and quiz score.

questions.source: Drill CH7 P2 — Pearson or Spearman?
questions.prompt: Both variables are RM amounts (ratio level). Which correlation coefficient, and why?
options: Pearson product-moment — both variables numeric/interval-ratio; Spearman is for ranked/ordinal data
questions.explain: **Pearson** for numeric interval/ratio data; **Spearman r_s** when data are RANKS (or get ranked). Stating the level-of-measurement reason earns the selection mark. Caution sentence: correlation ≠ causation.
r_s = 1 − 96/(8×63) = 1 − 96/504 = 1 − 0.190 = **0.810** — strong positive rank agreement (the manager's intuition largely matches real usage).

questions.source: Drill CH7 P4 — significance of r
questions.prompt: r = 0.72, n = 12. Compute t₀ = r/√((1−r²)/(n−2)) (2 decimals).
questions.explain: t₀ = 0.72/√(0.4816/10) = 0.72/0.21945 = **3.281**, df = n−2 = 10. vs t(0.025, 10) = 2.228 → reject H₀: significant correlation. At 99% (3.169) still rejects — but barely (margin 0.11).

questions.prompt: n = 7, Σx = 44, Σy = 34.5, Σx² = 370, Σxy = 251.1. Compute b₁ = (Σxy − ΣxΣy/n)/(Σx² − (Σx)²/n) (3 decimals).
ŷ = 2.625 + 0.367x. Predict ŷ at x = 7 (2 decimals).
questions.explain: ŷ(7) = 2.625 + 2.566 = **5.190** ≈ RM5,190/month. Keep ≥4 decimals mid-computation; round only at the end.

questions.prompt: The regression was fitted on temperatures 18–30°C. Why must you NOT predict sales at 40°C?
options: Extrapolation — the linear pattern is only supported inside the observed x range; beyond it the relationship may change
You can — regression is valid everywhere
questions.explain: **Extrapolation warning** (a guaranteed mark): predictions are reliable only within the observed range (18–30°C). ŷ(40) ≈ 285 would be unreliable — say 'should not be used'.

questions.prompt: SST = 13.434, SSE = 0.884. Compute R² = SSR/SST (3 decimals).
questions.explain: SSR = SST − SSE = 12.550 → R² = 12.550/13.434 = **0.934**. Sentence: '**93.4% of the variation in salary is explained by the variation in experience**; the remaining 6.6% is other factors.' Check: √0.934 = 0.967 ≈ r.

questions.prompt: Testing H₀: β₁ = 0 with t₀ = b₁/s_b₁ = 8.018/0.144 = 55.68, df = 5, critical 2.571. Verdict?
options: Reject H₀ — temperature has a statistically significant effect on sales
Fail to reject — the slope is too large
Reject H₀ — but only the intercept matters
The test is invalid because t > 10
questions.explain: 55.68 ≫ 2.571 → **reject H₀: β₁ ≠ 0** — significant linear relationship. The slope test (df = n−2) is exam Q5's final part; same 7-step structure as every other test.
